chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked about children? He said: Yes, he was asked, and he said: 'Allah knows best what they used to do.'

Then he said: O Zurarah, do you know what His saying 'Allah knows best what they used to do' means? I said: No. He said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has the choice regarding them. Indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, the children will be brought, and the old man who has reached old age but lost his intellect due to age and senility, and he who died in the period between prophets, and the madman and the simpleton who does not comprehend,

then each one of them will present a case for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah sends to them an angel from the angels, who kindles a fire and says: 'Indeed, your Lord commands you to jump into it.' Whoever jumps into it, it will be for him coolness and peace, and whoever disobeys him will be driven to the Fire.

key_terms.الْخَرَف: senility/loss of intellect due to old age

ai.seo_question: What happens to children and the mentally incapacitated on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'Al-Hujjah' (the divine proof) for those exempt from full accountability, including children, the senile, the mad, and those in the 'period of neglect' (Fatra). It interprets the Quranic verse 17:84 not merely as divine omniscience, but as a specific eschatological test where an angel commands them to jump into a fire; obedience results in the fire becoming 'cool and safe' for them, while disobedience leads to Hell, highlighting the role of free will even in those with limited intellect.
